content: Gestational Diabetes Mellitus (GDM) Recommendations by the American Diabetes Association (ADA): 1. Early Screening Before 15 Weeks of Gestation: It is recommended to perform early screening for individuals who present significant risk factors for diabetes or have undiagnosed diabetes at the beginning of pregnancy. This approach facilitates the early detection of hyperglycemia, enabling timely and appropriate interventions to mitigate potential complications. 2. Screening Between 24 and 28 Weeks of Gestation: For pregnant women who have not been previously diagnosed with diabetes, screening for GDM should be conducted during this period. The standard diagnostic method involves the administration of a 75-gram oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT), which is used to confirm the presence of gestational diabetes. 3. Postpartum Follow-Up: After delivery, women who were diagnosed with GDM during pregnancy should undergo a glucose tolerance test to assess their glucose metabolism. This follow-up is critical for identifying and managing any ongoing risk of developing type 2 diabetes in the future.
